title: Customers with repeat orders
prompt:
SQLite. Submit exactly one SELECT statement (a second, semicolon-separated statement is rejected).

Table:
  orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL)

Return one row per customer who placed at least 2 orders: the customer, and how many
orders they placed. The column names are part of the answer - name them exactly
customer and orders_count. Row order does not matter.

Example - for the rows
  (1, 'zoe', 10), (2, 'zoe', 4), (3, 'kai', 7)
the result is the single row  zoe | 2.
